## Understanding Offline Speech-to-Text


Offline speech-to-text converts spoken words into written text without a remote server, processing entirely on your device.


For most users, this comes down to privacy and reliability. Doctors may be transcribing in a hospital basement, on a flight, or in a rural clinic with no Wi-Fi. Lawyers work on trains or inside secure facilities where policy restricts internet access. Field researchers and journalists face the same constraint in remote locations. All of them share the same need: transcription that works and never ships voice data to the cloud.

## Superwhisper


[Superwhisper](https://willowvoice.com/comparison/superwhisper) offers offline transcription on Mac, Windows, and iOS, with latency around 900 ms to 2 seconds depending on model and hardware.

## Dragon Professional


Dragon Professional launched in 1997 as the first consumer continuous speech recognition product, and for nearly three decades it was the default answer for serious dictation software. That legacy is real. It has seen limited updates in recent years.


**✓ Strengths**

Fully offline local processing: audio never leaves your machine, making it one of the few tools with a decades-long track record of on-device dictation for compliance-sensitive Windows environments.


-


Deep PC control via a macro system: voice commands can launch programs, trigger application functions, and move through Windows entirely hands-free, well beyond what most modern dictation tools offer.


-


Accuracy can exceed 95% with multi-language support once a profile is fully trained, which helps users with extensive existing Dragon profiles who have already invested in the training process.


**Ideal for:** Windows users with existing Dragon profiles who need deep PC control beyond basic transcription.


**✗ Limitations**

The entry price is $699 one-time, and out-of-the-box accuracy is closer to 90%; reaching 95-97% takes weeks of active training. You also have to speak punctuation aloud ("period," "comma," "new paragraph"), which interrupts natural speaking rhythm and adds a layer of cognitive overhead that AI-native tools have eliminated.


Dragon is legacy tech with a steep setup cost. Willow Voice delivers accurate results from day one across Mac, Windows, and iOS, needs no training, and runs at ~200ms latency.

## Free Built-In Options for Offline Voice-to-Text


Not every use case requires a paid tool. Three built-in options offer offline voice-to-text at no cost, though each comes with meaningful constraints.


**Android offline voice typing (Gboard).** On any Android device, go to Settings > System > Languages & Input > Virtual Keyboard > Gboard > Voice Typing, turn on Offline speech recognition, and download your language pack. Transcription then runs on-device in any text field, with no internet required. Without vocabulary personalization, a learning loop, or compliance infrastructure, it falls short in professional workflows involving sensitive data or technical terminology.


**iOS offline voice input.** On iPhone and iPad, go to Settings > General > Keyboard > Turn On Dictation. From iOS 16, Apple processes voice input on-device for supported languages, so no audio leaves the device. In team contexts, on-device voice input carries no vocabulary or settings across apps or devices, offers no shared dictionaries or admin controls, and provides no compliance documentation trail for healthcare or legal environments.


**Windows Speech Recognition.** Built into Windows 10 and 11 under Settings > Time & Language > Speech, it runs entirely locally with no internet connection and supports voice commands for basic PC control alongside dictation. Accuracy lags behind AI-native tools, especially for technical vocabulary or accented speech, and the feature hasn't received substantive updates alongside the shift to AI-powered transcription engines.


These built-in options work for occasional use, but professionals who need accuracy, personalization, or compliance will need a dedicated tool.
